

Build a small, idiomatic Rust library of VDA 5050 v3.0.0 message types; no MQTT or fleet-control logic.
Use ../VDA5050/json_schemas/ and the matching specification as inputs. The Markdown specification is https://github.com/VDA5050/VDA5050/blob/main/VDA5050_EN.md; pin upstream provenance and flag discrepancies.
Reference https://github.com/kKdH/vda5050-types-rs for prior art, not as the v3 source of truth.
Keep dependencies minimal and discuss each addition before implementation; zero dependencies is not a goal at the expense of usability. Chrono is approved as a core dependency for `DateTime<Utc>` timestamp fields; minimize enabled features and verify Rust 1.85 compatibility.
Follow specification section 7.2 for timestamp wire encoding/decoding: ISO 8601 UTC `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.fffZ`, exactly three fractional digits and `Z`. Report invalid input or unrepresentable values without silent precision loss. Cite the pinned specification section in timestamp tests, including its example and format/precision boundaries.
Gate our message/model Serde implementations behind `serde` and JSON helpers behind `json` (enables `serde`). `serde_json` is an approved core dependency for JSON parameter values; its own Serde support is not gated by our feature.
Use a shared `ActionParameterValue` wrapper around `serde_json::Value` with a private inner value, checked construction rejecting top-level `null`, read-only access, and consuming extraction. Do not expose mutable access that bypasses the invariant. Reuse it in shared action parameters across order, instantActions, and zoneSet; preserve nested values permitted by the schema/specification. Feature-gated Serde support must enforce the same invariant and preserve the underlying wire shape.
Shared `Action` includes optional non-null `retriable` per specification section 7.3; section 7.4 reuses it even though the instant-actions schema omits that field. Order uses specification `maximumRotationSpeed`, not the pinned schema's `maxRotationSpeed` typo, without a decoding alias. Preserve pinned schemas unchanged and document such discrepancies.
Zone sets use a flattened typed `ZoneKind` enum with required variant parameters. Enforce at least three vertices in both Serde directions; defer topology, counterclockwise order, map bounds and protocol semantics. Require releaseLossBehavior per section 7.6/schema despite section 6.4.1's absent-value STOP prose. ZoneAction omits sender-supplied actionId and reuses shared blocking/parameter models; common Vertex is shared with factsheet, whose existing path remains a re-export.
Keep message bodies usable independently. Add dependency-free topic utilities and typed topic/body pairing behind an optional `topic` feature; topic-directed JSON helpers require both `topic` and `json`.
Model topic/body pairs, not MQTT packets or an invented JSON envelope. Support the suggested five-level topic layout explicitly, preserve mandatory topic names, and acknowledge broker-specific layouts. Exclude MQTT clients, network behavior, subscription operations, QoS, and session management. TopicFilter text helpers are approved: explicit interface, fixed v3 and whole-level + selectors only for manufacturer, serial and kind; no #, shared prefixes or matching/broker logic.
Use typed message variants to prevent topic-kind/body mismatches. Keep topic syntax checks separate from topic/header consistency validation, whose policy remains to be agreed. Implement bodies first, then topic support incrementally.
Preserve wire names, enum values, required/optional fields, and numeric constraints; distinguish deserialization from protocol validation.
Map specification integer types to matching Rust widths and test ranges with pinned specification citations, including endpoints, unsigned-negative input, overflow, and fractional input.
During deserialization, ignore unknown object fields (not preserved on re-encoding), reject unknown enum values, and reject missing required fields without defaults. Check schema/spec extension rules per message, record conflicts, and test these behaviors explicitly.
Accept explicit `null` only where the schema/specification explicitly allows it. Optional non-nullable fields use `Option<T>`: absence is `None`, valid presence is `Some`, and explicit `null` is rejected; omit `None` when encoding. Reuse shared Serde handling and test all three cases with pinned source citations.
Prefer explicit, documented public types and shared models; avoid unnecessary dependencies and generated-code complexity.
Handwrite public Rust types; schemas and the specification are design inputs, not library build/runtime dependencies. Do not generate types during builds. Pinned schemas may serve as dev/test fixtures for conformance checks without requiring a sibling checkout.
Use one module per message (`connection`, `factsheet`, `instant_actions`, `order`, `responses`, `state`, `visualization`, `zone_set`), with top-level message types re-exported at the crate root. Put genuinely shared models in `common` and message-specific supporting types in their message module. Gate the `topic` module behind its feature; do not add a `v3` namespace.
Embed a shared `common::Header` as a `header` field in message structs; flatten it under Serde to preserve top-level header fields on the wire.
Test all messages, wire compatibility, and feature combinations; maintain fmt, Clippy, tests, and rustdoc CI.
Keep public object decoding consistent for standalone, nested, and array-element use. Reuse the private object-model pattern rather than parent-only shape adapters. Preserve JSON float64 bits through text/byte round-trips with explicitly enabled `serde_json/float_roundtrip`; keep an independent consumer check so dev-dependency feature unification cannot hide regressions. Reuse cached schema/test helpers and include wire-field context in numeric errors.
Implement incrementally, one message/schema at a time, comparing each pinned schema with the matching specification sections before defining types.
For each message, add schema-derived wire/type tests and specification-derived cases for prose-only constraints, with pinned source citations; record discrepancies explicitly.
Keep schema conformance, deserialization, and semantic/protocol validation distinct. Tests must document what is enforced and what remains representable; do not introduce a validation API without agreeing on its scope.
Keep README examples, feature docs, badges, licensing, and publishing metadata accurate; discuss TODO.md decisions before implementation.
